newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIAN CLUBS VOTE AGAINST CHANGING SEASON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIAN CLUBS VOTE AGAINST CHANGING SEASON.

text.p: Most of Russia's top clubs have rejected a proposal to change the domestic calendar by bringing it into line with many Europe leagues.
They say the move would force teams to play in appalling weather conditions.
Boris Bobrov, executive director of Russia's professional league (PFL), said his executive council had almost unanimously thrown out the idea of moving to an autumn-spring season.

Vyacheslav Koloskov, president of the Russian soccer union (RFS), said earlier this week he supported an autumn-spring season to improve the country's recent disappointing record in European competitions.
A final decision will be taken in January when the RFS, which has overall control of Russian soccer, holds its annual conference in Moscow.
A handful of top clubs like Spartak Moscow and Alania Vladikavkaz -- who between them have won the last four Russian league titles -- support the change but the vast majority of clubs are against it.

The PFL -- which groups the premier as well as the first, second and third divisions -- said that given Russia's weather conditions, teams would be forced to play in a sea of mud in autumn and on bone-breakingly hard pitches in spring.
"Our stadiums, especially those in the provinces, are not well equipped to hold matches in the early spring and late autumn," Bobrov said.

"We have practically no stadiums with undersoil heating, which is dangerous for the players. This is not a simple question for Russia, because the climatic differences here are greater than those in the West."
RFS secretary general Vladimir Rodionov said the PFL could still be overruled.
"We'll hear the final word on this next January at the conference of the Russian soccer union. It will finally decide whether to change or not to change," he said.
The current season runs from early April to early November but this means that Russian clubs who qualify for European club competitions have to play the later rounds in what is their close season.
Few former Soviet clubs have enjoyed real European success but recent performances have been worse than usual.
Koloskov proposed the change after a number of reverses this season, especially Alania Vladikavkaz's 7-2 home thrashing by Glasgow Rangers in the preliminary round of the European Cup.

Russia has no covered soccer stadiums, although late last year Moscow mayor Yuri Luzhkov launched a plan to build a roof over the 100,000-seat Luzhniki stadium, which is currently home to Moscow Torpedo.
